terms.gloss: a council, a body of advisers
terms.comment: Counsel, and then the people who give it (Lewis & Short): a general’s council of war, the elders of Carthage, and the Roman senate itself, orbis terrae cōnsilium (Cic. Phil. 4.14). Morgan–Owens gives it for a committee or commission, and Egger for the Security Council, cōnsilium sēcūritātī tuendae.

terms.gloss: an assembly, a council of delegates
terms.comment: An assembly called together to take counsel, as the councils of the Gallic peoples in Caesar; Lewis & Short warn that the manuscripts often confuse it with cōnsilium. The usual word for a council of the Church (Morgan–Owens).

terms.gloss: a council of the Church, a synod
terms.comment: Greek σύνοδος: in inscriptions a college of priests, in late Latin an assembly of bishops (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: id erat sānctius apud illōs cōnsilium maximaque ad ipsum senātum regendum vīs
phrases.english: this was their more sacred council, with the greatest power to guide the senate itself (the thirty elders of Carthage)

phrases.latin: cōnsiliō celeriter convocātō sententiās exquīrere coepit
phrases.english: he quickly called a council and began to ask for opinions

sources: Lewis & Short: consilium · Lewis & Short: concilium · Lewis & Short: synodus
